original.target_description: Experiment 1, perspective contrast for positive-emotion passage reading times, p. 883 below Figure 1; least-squares comparison within the reading-time LMM described on p. 882 and in Table 1.

n.sample_role: Participants in the Experiment 1 reading-time LMM. Model also includes 24 stimulus items and 4431 sentence-level reading-time observations, separately.
n.exclusions: One of 36 recruited participants excluded for technical problems; 2.33% of reading-time data removed as outliers 2.5 SD below/above each participant’s mean sentence reading time.
n.location: p. 883 (PDF article p. 7), Table 1, NPart; pp. 881–882, Experiment 1 Participants and Results/Reading times.

notes: Identity assessment: the supplied text is the publisher-formatted primary article, matching title You’re the emotional one: the role of perspective for emotion processing in reading comprehension, authors Scarlett Child, Jane Oakhill and Alan Garnham, journal Language, Cognition and Neuroscience 33(7), 878–889 (2018), and DOI 10.1080/23273798.2018.1431397. It contains methods, results, tables, discussion and references, rather than only an abstract. No PDF path supplied; PDF rendering unavailable. NPart = 35 is explicitly printed in the critical reading-time model; NItem = 24 and Observations = 4431 identify separate stimulus-item and sentence-reading-time counting roles. Recruitment was 36 and one participant was excluded for technical problems (p. 881); 2.33% of reading-time data were removed as outliers at 2.5 SD below/above each participant’s mean sentence reading time (p. 882). No N derived from df or group sums. Targets were matched using study, outcome and named test, independently of row order or numeric matching. Only assigned n_o fields examined; other schema fields are placeholders. The positive-emotion perspective test is a conditional contrast from the common LMM, with perspective manipulated within participants. The reported participant count of that model is 35; a positive-only observation count is not separately printed, and is not inferred from df.
